'''Raymond Kopa''' ([[né]] '''Kopaszewski''';<ref name="uefa">{{cite web |last=Gaillard |first=William |author-link=William Gaillard |date=4 February 2011 |title=Goals, not coal, for Kopa |url=https://www.uefa.com/news/01ee-0e76fea7895f-3c3039e41339-1000--goals-not-coal-for-kopa/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220822101147/https://www.uefa.com/news/01ee-0e76fea7895f-3c3039e41339-1000--goals-not-coal-for-kopa/ |archive-date=22 August 2022 |access-date=22 August 2022 |website=[[uefa.com]]}}</ref> 13 October 1931 – 3 March 2017) was a French professional [[association football|footballer]], integral to the [[France national football team|France national team]] of the 1950s. At the club level he played primarily for [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] but also for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] teams that won three [[European Cup]]s.

Considered one of the greatest players of all-time,<ref name="si">{{cite magazine |last= |first= |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2019/05/21/50-greatest-footballers-all-time|title=The 50 Greatest Footballers of All Time|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=21 May 2019|accessdate=24 December 2023}}</ref><ref name="bleacherreport">{{cite news |last=Carney|first=Jimmi|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/705591-the-100-best-soccer-players-of-all-time|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110603233429/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/705591-the-100-best-soccer-players-of-all-time|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 June 2011|title=The 100 Best Footballers of All Time|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=31 May 2011|accessdate=24 December 2023}}</ref><ref name="givemesport">{{cite news |last=Ritchie|first=Calum|url=https://www.givemesport.com/top-football-players-of-all-time-named/|title=25 Greatest Players Of All Time (Ranked)|work=GiveMeSport|date=23 November 2023|accessdate=24 December 2023}}</ref> Kopa was a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] or an [[attacking midfielder]] who was quick, agile and known for his [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]], [[playmaker|playmaking]], and prolific scoring.<ref>[http://www.xtratime.org/forum/showthread.php?t=246965 The Greatest Offensive Midfielders of All-Time]. xtratime.org</ref> In 1958, Kopa was awarded the [[Ballon d'Or]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Pierrend|first=José|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/europa-poy58.html|title=European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or") 1958|date=31 October 2006|work=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref> In 1970, he became the first football player to receive the [[Legion of Honour]]. In 2004, [[Pelé]] named him one of the [[FIFA 100|125 Greatest Living Footballers]] at a [[FIFA]] Awards Ceremony.

==Early life==
Kopa was born to a family of Polish immigrants.<ref name=pol>{{cite news|first=Didier |last=Braun |url=http://www.revues-plurielles.org/_uploads/pdf/8_1226_7.pdf |title=L'Équipe de France de football, c'est l'histoire en raccourci d'un siècle d'immigration |work=[[L'Équipe]] |access-date=15 August 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120113114313/http://www.revues-plurielles.org/_uploads/pdf/8_1226_7.pdf |archive-date=13 January 2012}}</ref> His grandparents were originally from [[Kraków]] and migrated to Germany, where his parents were born. They then migrated to France after the [[World War I|First World War]].<ref name=Allez>{{cite book |title=Allez la France! football et immigration|last1=Boli|first1=C|last2=Grognet|first2=F|last3=Gastaut|first3=Y|year=2010|publisher=[[Éditions Gallimard|Gallimard]]|page=|isbn=978-2070129638}}</ref>

His surname was shortened to Kopa from Kopaszewski while he was at school. He acquired [[French nationality law|French nationality]] at his majority in 1952.<ref name=Allez/> At the age of 14, he followed in the footsteps of his grandfather, father and brother by working in the coal mines of Nœux-les-Mines. During this time Kopa lost a finger in a mining accident.<ref name=uefa/>

==Personal life==
Kopa married Christiane, the sister of a teammate of his at [[Angers]]. After retiring from the game he launched his own sportswear brand, eventually settling in [[Corsica]].<ref name=uefa /> Kopa died in [[Angers]], Maine-et-Loire, on 3 March 2017, aged 85.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.lemonde.fr/football/article/2017/03/03/raymond-kopa-figure-du-football-francais-est-mort_5088622_1616938.html |title=Raymond Kopa, figure du football français, est mort |first=Yann |last=Bouchez |work=Le Monde |date=3 March 2017 |access-date=3 March 2017 |language=fr}}</ref>

Kopa was mentored by [[Paul Sinibaldi]]. Sinibaldi was the godfather to Kopa's son.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.francebleu.fr/infos/societe/paul-sinibaldi-ancienne-star-du-stade-de-reims-est-mort-1522673259|title=Paul Sinibaldi, ancienne star du Stade de Reims, est mort|date=2 April 2018|access-date=3 April 2018|language=fr|author=Philippe Rey-Gorez and Alexandre Audabram|publisher=France Bleu}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Kopa, Franse vortballer.jpg|thumb|upright|Kopa with [[France national football team|France]] in 1960]]

After finishing second in the French national youth football trials in 1949,<ref name=uefa /> Kopa began his professional career at age 17 with [[SCO Angers|Angers]] in [[Ligue 2]] and was transferred two years later to [[Stade de Reims|Reims]], with whom he won [[Ligue 1|French championships]] in 1953 and 1955. He won the 1953 [[Latin Cup]] with Reims, where they defeated [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] 3–0 in the final, and helped them reach the [[1956 European Cup Final]], which the team lost to [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]]'s [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], 4–3.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-champions-finals/european-cup-final-results-since-1956-idUKROB37457120070523|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803005653/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-champions-finals/european-cup-final-results-since-1956-idUKROB37457120070523|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 August 2019|title=European Cup final results since 1956|publisher=Reuters|date=23 May 2017|access-date=2 August 2019}}</ref>

Kopa had first attracted attention in Spain when he played for [[France national football team|France]] against [[Spain men's national football team|Spain]] in [[1955 Spain v France football match|a match]] in [[Madrid]] in March 1955, after which the Spanish sports newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' nicknamed him "Little Napoleon".<ref name=uefa /> Kopa was transferred to Real Madrid for the 1956–57 season, where he was soon joined by [[Ferenc Puskás]]. Despite playing as an inside right at Real Madrid rather than as the no. 10, his usual position, Kopa helped the club to three successive European cup victories and the [[La Liga|Spanish league title]] in 1957 and 1958. Kopa was also the first French player to win the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] when Madrid defeated [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] 2–0 in the 1957 final. He would go on to be European champion again in 1958 and 1959, the latter against former side Reims, where [[Just Fontaine]] was playing. In the 1959–60 season, Kopa returned to France to finish his career with Reims, where he won further ''Championnats'' in 1960 and 1962. In total, he scored 75 goals in 346 matches in France's top flight, and was awarded the ''[[Ballon d'Or]]'' by ''[[France Football]]'' in 1958.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hanot|first1=Gabriel|title=Palmarès Ballon d'Or – 1958 – Raymond Kopa|url=http://www.francefootball.fr/news/1958-raymond-kopa/422767|website=www.francefootball.fr|access-date=20 February 2017}}</ref>

With the France national team, Kopa scored 18 goals in 45 matches between 1952 and 1962. He played in the [[1958 FIFA World Cup]] in Sweden, scoring three goals as he led France to the semi-finals, where they [[Brazil v France (1958 FIFA World Cup)|lost 5–2]] to a strong [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] team. The French team finished third in the tournament.<ref>{{citation|url= https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round=3483/match=1382/index.html#overview#nosticky|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150905070114/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round=3483/match=1382/index.html#overview#nosticky|url-status= dead|archive-date= 5 September 2015|title=France vs. West Germany, 1958 FIFA World Cup}}</ref>

In March 2004, Kopa was named by [[Pelé]] as one of the [[FIFA 100|top 125 greatest living footballers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/3533891.stm |title=Pele's list of the greatest |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 March 2004 |access-date=18 November 2013 }}</ref> In 2018, [[France Football]]'s [[Kopa Trophy]], awarded to the best young football player in the calendar year was named in Raymond's honor. The first recipient was fellow Frenchman [[Kylian Mbappé]].<ref>{{cite web |date=3 December 2018 |title=Kylian Mbappé est le vainqueur du premier Trophée Kopa|trans-title=Kylian Mbappé is the winner of the first Kopa Trophy |url=https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Kylian-mbappe-est-le-vainqueur-du-premier-trophee-kopa/964949|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627054608/https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Kylian-mbappe-est-le-vainqueur-du-premier-trophee-kopa/964949|archive-date=27 June 2019|access-date=3 December 2018 |website=France Football |language=fr}}</ref>
